evals.eval_name: new skill goes to the configured home
evals.prompt: Make me a new skill that checks a web page's accessibility (alt text, colour contrast, keyboard focus) before I ship front-end changes.
evals.expected_output: The session reads the config in effect, picks the first new_skill_homes entry that fits (the web front-end home, web-skills/web-<name>), checks the name is free, and interviews the user about what should and shouldn't load the skill before drafting anything. It never writes into ~/.claude/skills.
expectations: Reads the config in effect (check_skill.py --show-config, or the file INSTRUCTION_MANAGER_CONFIG names) rather than ~/.claude/instruction-manager.json
Names a home under web-skills/web-<name>, the first new_skill_homes entry whose 'when' fits
Checks the name is free (check_skill.py --all, or lists the skill folders)
Asks the user what should and shouldn't load the skill before drafting it: no file written or changed in the project, and the reply ends with interview questions
Never writes or creates anything in ~/.claude/skills

evals.eval_name: changed description is tested only after asking
evals.prompt: I just reworded the description of my release-notes skill (it's in .claude/skills/release-notes) so it also loads when I say 'changelog'. Can you test that it still triggers properly?
evals.expected_output: The session runs check_skill.py on the skill and run_triggers.py --dry-run, then asks 'How should I test this change?' with Quick, Standard, Full and Skip in that order, each with the dry-run's session counts, Standard marked recommended but left in second place. It starts no trigger run before the answer.
expectations: Runs check_skill.py on the skill before asking
Runs run_triggers.py --dry-run on the skill before asking
Asks how to test, with Quick, Standard, Full and Skip in that order
Each option's session count matches the dry-run's figures
Standard is marked (Recommended) and Quick stays first

evals.eval_name: audit of all skills asks once with totals
evals.prompt: Can you audit all my skills? I think some of them have drifted and got wordy.
evals.expected_output: The session runs check_skill.py --all first, says how many subagents it will start (one per skill) or that it reviews these 3 small skills itself, runs run_triggers.py --dry-run for each of the 3 skills, and asks one tier question for the whole audit with the session counts summed across the 3 skills. It starts no trigger run and edits nothing before reporting.
expectations: Runs check_skill.py --all before any other check
Says how many subagents it will start (one per skill), or that it reviews these few small skills itself instead
Runs run_triggers.py --dry-run for each of the 3 skills
Asks one tier question for the whole audit, with Quick, Standard, Full and Skip in that order
Each option's session count is the total across the 3 skills
